report.summary: The application is experiencing frequent and significant CPU spikes, consistently exceeding the 16.67ms target for 60 frames per second. Accompanying these spikes are moderate to high garbage collection allocations (112KB to 154KB per spike), indicating potential memory churn. This combination likely results in noticeable stuttering and a suboptimal user experience.

bottlenecks.description: Consistent CPU frame times exceeding 18ms, frequently reaching over 20ms and even 24ms, indicate that the game is failing to meet its target frame rate (e.g., 60 FPS requires ~16.67ms). This could be due to heavy rendering, complex physics, expensive script logic, or inefficient algorithm execution occurring every frame or very frequently.
bottlenecks.solution: Profile deeper using the Unity Profiler to identify specific CPU-bound operations. Common culprits include: 1. Rendering: Too many draw calls, overdraw, expensive shaders, unoptimized lighting. Use the Frame Debugger to analyze rendering. 2. Physics: Overly complex colliders, too many rigidbodies, frequent physics queries. Optimize physics layers and reduce complexity. 3. Scripts: Expensive loops, frequent GetComponent calls, inefficient data structures, unnecessary calculations in `Update`/`LateUpdate`. Optimize algorithms and cache references. 4. UI: Complex UI hierarchies, frequent layout recalculations. 5. Unoptimized asset loading during gameplay.

bottlenecks.description: Persistent garbage collection allocations ranging from 112KB to 154KB per spike are occurring. Even seemingly small allocations, if frequent, will trigger the garbage collector more often, causing performance hitches and stuttering. The variability in allocation size (e.g., 112KB vs 154KB) suggests multiple sources or conditionally allocated memory.
bottlenecks.solution: Identify the source of memory allocations using the Unity Profiler's Memory module or by adding `GC.GetTotalMemory(true)` logs. Common causes include: 1. String operations: Excessive string concatenations, `ToString()` calls. Use `StringBuilder` or pre-format strings. 2. LINQ: LINQ queries often create temporary collections and closures. Avoid in performance-critical paths. 3. Boxing: Converting value types to object types. 4. Collections: Creating new lists/arrays frequently instead of pooling or reusing them. 5. Coroutines: Yielding `new WaitForSeconds()` creates new objects. Cache these or use custom yield instructions. 6. Unity API calls: Some Unity APIs (e.g., `Camera.main`, `GameObject.name`, `Mesh.vertices`) can allocate if called frequently. Cache or optimize access.
